## 1. Component structure and the ui-kits layering

### What moved where

Your `footer/index.tsx` held five components in 561 lines. Your `theme/components/footer.ts` held one 35-part recipe covering all of them. `5ecd515` split **both files along the same seams at the same time** — each component got its own folder, and its slice of the recipe moved to sit beside it.

| Was (all inside `footer/index.tsx`) | Now |
|---|---|
| `Footer` (named export) | `footer/index.tsx:56` — same name, now pure assembly |
| `FooterContainer` (default export) | `footer/index.tsx:160`, `export default` at `:207` |
| `BottomBar` (module-private) | `footer/bottomBar/index.tsx:30` — now `export const` |
| *inline JSX in `Footer`'s `navGroups.map`* | `footer/footerNavColumn/index.tsx:34` — **new component** |
| `ContactIconRow` (module-private) | `ui-kits/molecules/zimmContactIconRow/index.tsx:48` → `ZimmContactIconRow` |
| `SubscribeSection` (module-private) | `ui-kits/organisms/zimmSubscribeSection/index.tsx:40` → `ZimmSubscribeSection` |
| `SubscribeModal` (module-private) | **split in two** — content → `ui-kits/organisms/zimmSubscribeModal/index.tsx:35`; portal/backdrop/dialog chrome → `ui-kits/atoms/zimmModal/index.tsx:33` (**new**) |
| the subscribe state machine (inline `useState`) | `overrides/app/hooks/useSubscribeSection.ts` (**new**) |
| `useSubscribeModal.ts` | `overrides/app/hooks/useZimmModal.ts` (git-detected rename, R056) |

Two components are genuinely new: **`ZimmModal`** (the dialog chrome, extracted so any organism can reuse it) and **`FooterNavColumn`** (promoted out of inline JSX).

### The rule that decided placement

Two axes, and only the second is the atomic-design one.

**Axis 1 — does it know it's a footer?** If yes it stays in `footer/`. `FooterNavColumn` takes a `FooterNavGroupEntry`; `BottomBar` renders the copyright line and locale placeholder. Both are footer-local. Everything else moved to `ui-kits/`, each carrying a JSDoc line stating the reuse claim explicitly — e.g. `zimmContactIconRow/index.tsx:43-45`: *"Extracted from the footer so it can be reused anywhere a storefront needs the same channels — nothing here is footer-specific."*

**Axis 2 — composition depth, within `ui-kits/`:**

- **atom** — composes no other ui-kits component. `ZimmModal` renders `createPortal` plus two `chakra.div`s.
- **molecule** — composes atoms only. `ZimmContactIconRow` imports `ZimmIcon` and nothing above it.
- **organism** — composes molecules and/or owns real state. `ZimmSubscribeSection` imports `ZimmInputAction` and drives `useSubscribeSection`.

### Co-located styles: the mechanism

This is the part most worth understanding properly, because the *consumption* side didn't change at all and that's easy to misread as "nothing changed."

> **Was:** recipe in `theme/components/<name>.ts` → registered in `theme/components/index.ts` → consumed by name.
> **Now:** recipe in `<componentFolder>/<name>.css.ts` → **still registered in `theme/components/index.ts`** → consumed by name.

The only thing that changed is where the file sits — and, separately, who has to approve it (§6).

Why it's a runtime no-op: `useMultiStyleConfig` resolves against `theme.components[key]`, and **the key is the object's property name in the `components` map, not the filename.** So moving the file changes nothing as long as the barrel still exports it under the same key. Every recipe key is in fact unchanged — `Button`, `ZimmNavItem`, `ZimmTextInput` all kept their names.

A worked example, end to end:

```ts
// overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmContactIconRow/zimmContactIconRow.css.ts:1
export const ZimmContactIconRow = {
  parts: ['row', 'iconLink'],
  baseStyle: { /* ... */ },
};
```

```ts
// overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts:8, then :22
import { ZimmContactIconRow } from 'app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmContactIconRow/zimmContactIconRow.css';
export const components = { /* ... */, ZimmContactIconRow, /* ... */ };
```

```tsx
// overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmContactIconRow/index.tsx
const ZIMM_CONTACT_ICON_ROW_RECIPE = 'ZimmContactIconRow';        // :6
const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_CONTACT_ICON_ROW_RECIPE, {});  // :49
<chakra.div __css={styles.row}>                                   // :56
```

Note the import specifier ends `.css`, not `.css.ts` — extension resolution supplies the `.ts`. It reads like a CSS import and isn't one. This resolves in all three toolchains because webpack, Vitest and Storybook each put `.ts` first in their resolve order or alias `app` → `overrides/app`.

All seven new components follow exactly this shape: a `const ZIMM_*_RECIPE` string at the top, one `useMultiStyleConfig` call, `__css={styles.<part>}` at each node.

**One deliberate exception to one-recipe-per-component:** `ZimmSubscribeModal` reads *two* recipes — its own content parts plus `ZimmModal`'s chrome (`zimmSubscribeModal/index.tsx:9-10`, consumed at `:97`). The atom owns overlay/panel/actions; each consuming organism owns title/fields/copy. So `ZimmModal.actions` is styled by the atom and rendered by the organism.

### What's left in `theme/components/`

Six files: `footerShared.ts` (new — the two cross-file values, `BP` breakpoints and `SIZE_COL_NAV`), `header.ts`, `index.ts`, `listMenu.ts`, `navConstants.ts`, `recipeGuards.test.ts`.

`footer.ts`, `button.ts`, `zimmNavItem.ts` and `zimmTextInput.ts` are gone — moved, not emptied, with no re-export shims. There are no stale imports anywhere in the repo.

> **Was:** the theme tree was a leaf — nothing in `theme/` imported from `app/components/`.
> **Now:** `theme/components/index.ts` is a mixed barrel. Four entries still use relative `./` paths (`header`, `listMenu`); eight import via the `app/components/...` alias. **The dependency arrow between those two layers is reversed.**

There is no cycle today — every `.css.ts` imports only Chakra types or `footerShared`, and that was checked across all ten of them. But a single component import inside a future `.css.ts` creates a real one and drags React into the theme bundle.

### Nothing broke

Worth stating plainly, because a 35-file refactor of shared components is exactly where you'd expect breakage:

- **No prop shape changed** on any extracted component. The four extracted prop types are field-for-field identical to their originals; only the type names changed.
- **No default↔named export flips.**
- **Every recipe key is unchanged.**
- SFCC's own base `_app` imports `app/components/footer` and renders the **default** export with no props — still `FooterContainer`, still with `data` optional by omission.

### Two real behaviour changes bundled into the "refactor" commits

Both are improvements, both documented in-file, but neither is a pure move:

- **The subscribe section now distinguishes failure from success.** Your version rendered `styles.subscribeSuccess` for `'unavailable'` and `'error'` too. There's now a dedicated coral `error` part (`zimmSubscribeSection.css.ts:51-55`) with `role="alert"` on that branch. That's the 36th recipe part and the only genuinely new styling in the set.
- **The focus trap gained a containment branch.** `useZimmModal.ts:100`:

  ```ts
  if (!(active instanceof Node) || !trapRef.current.contains(active)) {
    (e.shiftKey ? last : first).focus();
  ```

  This is the exact defect CodeRabbit raised on `useSubscribeModal` and you deferred to HPC-035 — focus arriving from outside the focusable set no longer escapes the dialog. **That HPC-035 item can be closed.**

> **Was:** `useSubscribeModal`, exposing `formRef: RefObject<HTMLFormElement>`.
> **Now:** `useZimmModal`, exposing `trapRef: RefObject<HTMLElement>` — hence the `trapRef as React.RefObject<HTMLFormElement>` cast at `zimmSubscribeModal/index.tsx:61`.

---

## 2. Contentful data flow

### The content model — five types, all reference-linked

All live in `scripts/contentful/content-types/`, one file per type. Nothing is nested or embedded; every relationship is a reference array.

**`region`** is the keystone and the most useful new idea. One entry per storefront, with `siteId` (required, unique), a human `label`, and a `locale` field that is explicitly informational only. Its comment states the contract: `siteId` matches an SFCC site ID from `contentfulMapping.generated.ts`'s `SITE_LOCALES` keys. Because it's a real referenceable entity, **nothing else in the model carries a hardcoded site list.**

**`link`** — `label` (localised) + `href` (not localised) + optional `regions`. Deliberately generic; its description says it's designed to be referenced from header nav and mega-menu later without change.

**`footerNavGroup`** — one column: `heading` (localised), a required `links` array, and a `showContactChannels` boolean.

> That boolean is a genuinely good modelling call and the comment says why (`footerNavGroup.js:9-10`): it's *"A flag, not a heading match — heading is localised, so matching its text breaks per storefront."* Matching `heading === 'Contact'` would have died silently the first time an editor typed "Kontakt".

**`footerConfig`** — the root. `internalTitle` (the `displayField`), `subscribeHeading`/`subscribeBody`, required `navGroups`, optional `legalLinks`, `copyrightOwner`, the three contact channels, and its own optional `regions`.

**`uiCopy`** — one entry per UI string. Covered in §3.

An editor building an AU footer creates `link` entries, groups them into `footerNavGroup` entries, then references those from a `footerConfig` — three levels of reference-picking, using the standard Contentful UI at each level. The `internalTitle`/`title` fields exist purely so the entry list is scannable.

### Region resolution — two stages, and the split matters

The mechanism lives in `overrides/app/utils/resolveByRegion.ts` and is deliberately not footer-specific — it accepts anything shaped `{fields: {regions?: [{fields: {siteId}}]}}`.

Two rules:

- **Eligibility** (`:22-26`) — an entry with omitted or empty `regions` matches **every** site. Otherwise it matches only if some region's `siteId` equals the current site.
- **Specificity** (`:29-30`) — `regions.length` where non-empty, else `Infinity`. Fewer regions = more specific; global sorts last.

Two exported functions apply those rules differently, and this is the part to internalise:

- **`pickMostSpecificByRegion`** (`:52`) — **single winner.** Used to choose *which* `footerConfig` renders.
- **`filterByRegion`** (`:37`) — **inclusive.** Keeps every eligible entry. Used for arrays where multiple regional entries legitimately coexist, e.g. links inside a shared nav group.

Ties between two equally-scoped non-global entries resolve by most-recently-updated with a `console.warn` (`:71-79`). The comment is honest about why: nothing in an additive-only pipeline prevents two entries both scoping to exactly `['ZimmermannUS']`.

`scopeToRegion` (`footer/index.tsx:132-144`) is the second stage — it maps over `navGroups` running `filterByRegion` on each group's `links`, and over `legalLinks`. Its docstring explains the need: Contentful's `include`-resolved response nests the graph but applies no region scoping of its own.

### The flow, end to end

```
Contentful CDA (cdn.contentful.com)
  │  contentful SDK client, memoised
  ├─ overrides/app/hooks/useContentfulClient.ts:44   createClient({space, environment, accessToken, host})
  │
  ├─ overrides/app/components/footer/index.tsx:183   useEffect → getEntries({content_type:'footerConfig', include:3})
  ├─ overrides/app/utils/resolveByRegion.ts:52       pickMostSpecificByRegion(configs, site.id)     ← ONE winner
  ├─ overrides/app/components/footer/index.tsx:132   scopeToRegion → filterByRegion over links      ← MANY kept
  │
  └─ <Footer data={footerData}>                      footer/index.tsx:204
       ├─ ZimmSubscribeSection    heading/body from subscribeHeading/subscribeBody
       ├─ FooterNavColumn         one per navGroup, + the three contact hrefs
       │    ├─ links.map → ZimmNavItem                    footerNavColumn/index.tsx:57
       │    └─ showContactChannels && <ZimmContactIconRow> footerNavColumn/index.tsx:89
       └─ BottomBar               copyright + legalItems
```

`include: 3` is the Contentful link-resolution depth: the CDA walks references three levels down and returns the whole graph in one response, rather than the client making a request per link. Three is what this model needs — `footerConfig` → `navGroups` → `links` → `regions`.

**`site.id` comes from `useMultiSite()`** (`footer/index.tsx:170-173`).

### The container/presentational split, and where it bends

`FooterContainer` (`:160-205`) is the default export and does the fetching. The presentational `Footer` (`:56`) is a named export taking `data` as a required prop and fetching nothing. `FooterNavColumn`, `BottomBar` and `ZimmSubscribeSection` are all pure prop-consumers.

So the split is real. But the fetch does sit inside a component under `overrides/app/components/`, which `components.md` reserves for containers — and the code flags this itself at `:156-158`:

> *"Note this puts a fetch inside `components/`, which components.md reserves for containers; if that matters, this should move into an `_app` override instead (Tier 2 shared shell — coordinate first)."*

The justification is legitimate: base `_app/index.jsx` renders `<Footer />` with no props, so there is no upstream container to own the data. Note that `542ac65`'s rule addition does **not** legitimise this — it carves out an exception for Context-backed copy hooks, not for a component-level fetch. This remains knowingly-accepted debt.

### Rendering: client-only

> **Was:** the footer rendered from a static fixture, so it was present in the server-rendered HTML.
> **Now:** it fetches in a `useEffect`, and `footer/index.tsx:202` is `if (!footerData) return null;` — so on the server `footerData` is `null` and **the footer is absent from the SSR HTML entirely**, appearing only after hydration plus a client round-trip.

I verified this directly: the `useEffect` fetch, the null return at line 202, and the absence of any `getProps` anywhere in the footer path.

### Failure behaviour — two deliberately opposite policies

## 3. The copy system

### What it is now

`useUiCopy` is one line:

```ts
// overrides/app/hooks/useUiCopy.ts:38
export const useUiCopy = (): UiCopyContextValue => useContext(UiCopyContext) ?? FALLBACK_ONLY;
```

The contract is `{ t: (key: string, fallback: string) => string; isLoading: boolean }`. **Both `t` parameters are required** — TypeScript won't let you call `t('some.key')` without a fallback. That one decision is what makes every failure mode collapse to a single behaviour.

Real call sites:

```tsx
// overrides/app/components/footer/bottomBar/index.tsx:35-36
const { t } = useUiCopy();
const copyrightLabel = t('footer.copyright.label', 'Copyright');
```

Five keys are in use today: `footer.copyright.label` and `footer.subscribe.{emailLabel,buttonLabel,successMessage,unavailableMessage}`.

The Provider is mounted innermost in `_app-config/index.tsx:161`:

```tsx
<UiCopyProvider>{children}</UiCopyProvider>
```

Because `_app-config` wraps the entire app *including* the base template's `_app` (which owns `IntlProvider`), `UiCopyProvider` sits **above** `IntlProvider` — so `useUiCopy` is genuinely available everywhere.

### Why it was built twice in one day

This is the most instructive seam in the branch, and the reason is mechanical.

The hook underneath is **not React Query.** `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts:88-156` is a hand-rolled `useState` + `useEffect` + `fetch`. There is no cache, no dedup, no query key. **Two components calling it meant two identical CDA round-trips; ten meant ten.**

So commit 10's prop-drilling wasn't stylistic distaste avoided — it *was* the mitigation. `FooterContainer` called the hook once and threaded five resolved strings into `Footer`, which passed one down to `BottomBar` and four to `ZimmSubscribeSection`. Ten new optional props across three prop types. Tim's own commit message names it: *"neither double-fetches since only the container calls the hook."*

That mitigation only works while there is exactly one consumer. Any second consumer anywhere — header, PDP, checkout — would have needed its own container-level fetch or its own prop chain.

Commit 12 inverted it. The fetch, the map build and `t` moved verbatim into `UiCopyProvider`; the hook became `useContext`. All ten props were deleted, and two long message constants that had been *exported from the leaf* so the container could reuse them as fallbacks went back to module-private (`zimmSubscribeSection/index.tsx:12-13`).

**In one sentence:** commit 10 avoided the redundant-fetch problem by funnelling through one caller; commit 12 eliminated it by sharing one fetch, which then made direct calls from anywhere safe.

Explicitly *not* the reasons: no SSR mismatch was being fixed (both versions are client-only), and no React Query cache problem existed, because React Query was never in this path.

### The load-bearing design decision

With no Provider mounted, `useUiCopy()` **does not throw**:

```ts
// overrides/app/hooks/useUiCopy.ts:19-22
const FALLBACK_ONLY: UiCopyContextValue = {
  t: (_key: string, fallback: string) => fallback,
  isLoading: false,
};
```

That's what lets a leaf call the hook with zero Storybook decorators and zero Vitest setup. `footer/index.test.tsx:24-27` documents deliberately *removing* a mock because of it.

The trade: **missing key, still loading, network down, and no provider are all indistinguishable** — same silent fallback, nothing in the console, and each is separately tested to produce the identical outcome.

### Keys, and how this relates to react-intl

Keys are free-form dot-path strings — `<area>.<component>.<thing>` — with **no typed union, no generated key type, no enum**. Uniqueness is enforced CMS-side only. Nothing verifies that a key referenced in code exists in Contentful, or vice versa.

The relationship to the existing i18n setup is the thing to get straight, because they are **parallel mechanisms and `useUiCopy` bypasses react-intl** rather than complementing it. react-intl comes from the untouched base `_app` via `IntlProvider` fed by React Query, with messages compiled from `translations/`. Only two files under `overrides/` actually import `useIntl`.

Three differences that matter:

| | react-intl | `useUiCopy` |
|---|---|---|
| **Locale** | resolves per storefront | **no locale is passed at all** |
| **SSR** | messages arrive via React Query, so translated text is in the server HTML | resolves in `useEffect`; server emits the English fallback, text swaps after hydration |
| **Governance** | `translations/` is Tier 2, Integration-owned, needs a PR | a Contentful editor changes production copy with no code change and no review |

**Decision rule, as the code actually behaves:** needs to be editable by a content editor without a deploy → `uiCopy`. Needs to be correct in the SSR HTML, vary by locale *today*, already exist in the base catalogue, or interpolate a variable → react-intl.

Nothing prevents the same label existing in both systems, and nothing detects it.

### The `uiCopy` content type

Four fields: `title` (required, non-localised, and the `displayField`), `key` (required, unique, non-localised — *"Must be identical across locales to work as a map key"*), `value` (required, **localised**), `description` (optional, translator context).

`title` was added by commit 11 purely for the editor: `displayField` was `key`, so Studio's entry list rendered raw dot-paths and became unscannable past a handful of entries. The runtime only ever reads `key` and `value`.

Two properties of the model worth knowing: `value` is a **`Symbol`, not `Text`**, so Contentful caps it at 256 characters and there's no rich text — and `t()` returns a raw string with no ICU interpolation, so a string needing a variable can't live here at all.

### Localisation is modelled but not wired

`subscribeHeading`, `subscribeBody`, `heading`, `label` and `value` are all declared `localized: true`. But **no locale is ever passed at runtime** — not by `createClient` (`useContentfulClient.ts:46`), not by the footerConfig query (`footer/index.tsx:183`), not by the uiCopy fetch (`useContentful.ts:110`). I verified this directly.

So **every storefront currently receives the space's default locale (`en`) for all localised footer and uiCopy fields.** The `uiCopy` content type's own description claims entries are fetched *"one CDA call per locale"*; the implementation makes one call with no locale. That description is aspirational, not descriptive.

## 4. Token policy

### The new rule

Hierarchy point 2 of `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md:16-27` was rewritten in place:

> 2. **Raw `var(--zimm-*)` CSS custom properties** for colour and spacing — `color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)"`, `gap="var(--zimm-scale-m)"`. **Never** a bare Chakra/theme token string (`color="text.default"`, `gap="m"`) — even though `theme.colors`/`theme.space` ARE registered from the same Zimmermann foundations […] and a bare key resolves to the identical value. This is a house-style requirement, not a correctness one: a `var(--zimm-*)` reference is unambiguous at every call site, where a bare key forces a PR reviewer to check `theme/index.ts`'s registered-scale list to know whether it happens to be correct.

> **Was:** bare semantic token strings were the recommended second tier — `color="text.default"`, `spacing="m"`.
> **Now:** they're forbidden for colour and spacing. `var(--zimm-*)` is mandatory, in recipes **and** in JSX/`sx`.

Concretely, from `bottomBar.css.ts`:

```ts
// before                              // now (:7, :55, :109, :112)
backgroundColor: 'background.06',      backgroundColor: 'var(--zimm-color-bg-06)',
paddingY: 'xs',                        paddingY: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)',
color: 'text.inverse',                 color: 'var(--zimm-color-text-inverse)',
gap: '2xs',                            gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-2xs)',
```

**Scope is colour and spacing only.** Typography stays at point 1 — `textStyle="body2"`, never a raw `fontSize`. `textStyle` remains a bare key and is the one documented exception, because there's no `var(--zimm-*)` substitute for the composite expansion itself. Sizing props aren't mentioned by the new rule at all.

> **Was:** `var(--zimm-*)` belonged in theme recipes and never in component JSX.
> **Now:** `css.md` shows `<Box color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)" padding="var(--zimm-scale-m)" />` as the ✅ example **in component JSX**. `footerNavColumn/index.tsx:44` and `:62` carry `paddingLeft: 'var(--zimm-scale-2xs)'` in an inline `__css` merge. This is a deliberate reversal of the position you had recorded as settled.

### Why it's a workaround, and why that's the right call

The two traps you documented are **untouched**. `theme/index.ts` is byte-identical across all 14 commits. `fontSizes`, `lineHeights`, `letterSpacings` and `sizes` remain unregistered. The live instance at `header/index.tsx:302` (`fontSize="l"`, which emits nothing) is still there.

But **"fix" was never available**, and the file says why (`theme/index.ts:31-39`):

> Deliberately NOT registered, because the Zimmermann scale and the Chakra scale use the same key names for different values — remapping them would silently restyle the base retail-react-app, which uses those names at ~199 call sites

Registering `fontSizes` *is* the breakage. Given that, the `var(--zimm-*)` mandate is a structurally effective mitigation: `width: 'var(--zimm-scale-m)'` performs **no `theme.sizes` lookup at all** — Chakra passes the string through and the browser resolves the custom property. The 8×–112× misresolution has no opportunity to occur at any call site that adheres.

Two caveats:

- **The policy doesn't cover the props where the traps live.** A bare spacing key on `width` isn't a violation of the new rule; it's caught only by the *pre-existing* guard at `recipeGuards.test.ts:295`, which predates this range.
- **There is no `--zimm-font-size-l`.** The font-size vars are only `md`, `xs`, `2xs`, `3xs`, `4xs`. So `header:302` has no var-based remedy — the correct fix there is `textStyle`.

He replaced `resolveBaseStyle` — which invoked a function-form `baseStyle` **once**, with all booleans false — with `resolveAllBaseStyles`, which enumerates all **2⁵ = 32** combinations of `inverse`/`disabled`/`hasError`/`focused`/`filled`.

That's a real hole closed in a guard you wrote, and it isn't in the commit subject.


1. **Stop writing `color="text.default"` / `gap="m"` / `padding="m"`.** Use `var(--zimm-color-*)` and `var(--zimm-scale-*)`, in recipes **and** in JSX/`sx`. `npm run test` fails you inside a registered recipe; in JSX nothing catches it.
2. **`textStyle` is the one exception** — `textStyle="body2"`, never a raw `fontSize`.
3. **New component styling goes in a co-located `<name>.css.ts`**, not `theme/components/`. Register it in `theme/components/index.ts` regardless of where the file lives.
4. **Cross-file shared style values go in a module that stays in `theme/components/`** — the `footerShared.ts` precedent. Don't copy a literal into two co-located files.
5. **Run `npm run audit:tokens` before any PR** touching `overrides/app/components/**` or `overrides/app/theme/components/**`. It's not in CI, and it currently exits 1 on 14 pre-existing findings — so read the list rather than trusting the exit code. If a raw value is genuinely unavoidable, put `provisional`, `pending`, `placeholder`, or `audit-allow: <reason>` in the surrounding comment block.
6. **Every logic-heavy component needs its own `index.test.ts(x)`** in its own folder. A `play` function — yours or a parent's — no longer satisfies the check.
7. **Mock `ZimmIcon` in any test rendering an icon-consuming component.** Don't try to fix it in `vitest.config.ts` without deciding to touch Tier 1.
8. **You may call `useUiCopy()` / `useIntl()` from a leaf.** Any other data-fetching hook still belongs in a page or container.
9. **Contentful schema changes are two commands:** `npm run sync:contentful`, then `npm run install:contentful -- --target <env>` per environment. Run `npm run env -- init` first to pick up `CONTENTFUL_ORGANIZATION_ID`.
10. **Touching `overrides/app/components/uiCopyProvider/` is now a Tier 2 change.**

---

# ⛔ PART 2 — ASSESSMENT

> **Everything above this line is a neutral description of how the system works. Everything below is judgement.**
>
> If you share this document, share Part 1 only. Part 2 contains criticism of a colleague's unreviewed work-in-progress and is written for your decision-making, not for circulation.

---

## Six cross-cutting patterns

These only become visible when the domains are stacked. Each is one root cause with several symptoms that look unrelated in isolation.

### 1. Hand-maintained mirrors are drifting

Tier classification now lives in **four** places. Two were updated:

| Source | Says about `UiCopyProvider` |
|---|---|
| `protectedFiles.md:19` | Tier 2 ✅ |
| `CODEOWNERS:93` | Tier 2 ✅ |
| `generateRegistry.mjs:140` `TIER2_PATHS` | **not updated** — hardcoded mirror |
| `.claude/registry/components.md` | **"4 — Feature-local"** ❌ |

Because `TIER2_PATHS` is a hardcoded array rather than a parse of the rules files, **regenerating the registry reproduces the wrong tier.** It needs `'app/components/uiCopyProvider/'` added to that array.

The same root cause, elsewhere:

- **`syncCursorRules.mjs`'s manifest omits `components.md`, `css.md` and `overrideStyling.md` entirely.** So the `var(--zimm-*)` mandate and the hook exception — the two largest rule changes in the branch — **reach Claude Code only.** Anyone using Cursor or Copilot on this codebase is working from the pre-inversion rules.
- **`seedRegions.mjs` carries a static copy** of the site list from `contentfulMapping.generated.ts`, with a comment acknowledging it can drift.
- **`useZimmModal` now has 5 consumers**, which meets `protectedFiles.md`'s own stated "Shared Hooks — 5+ consumers" threshold for Tier 2. It wasn't added to the list or to CODEOWNERS.

### 2. The gate was removed before the replacement was built

A chain, every link verified:

1. `CODEOWNERS:186` strips the Tier 1/2 approver from every `.css.ts` under `overrides/app/components/`.
2. The named replacement — `audit:tokens` as a required CI check — **does not exist**.
3. It *cannot* be wired yet: it currently **exits 1 on 14 pre-existing violations**.
4. Triage isn't purely mechanical either — `header.ts`'s `min(597px, 60vw)` is deliberate fluid sizing with no token form, so it needs an `audit-allow`, not a fix. That slightly undercuts the "just needs triage" framing in the docs.
5. Meanwhile `overrideStyling.md:188` still cites `button.ts` as the example of a value that *"stays behind the full gate"* — the exact file `a063e14` moved out from behind it, **24 minutes after that sentence was written**.

**Net effect:** `zimmButton.css.ts:243` exports `Button` — the recipe key that styles **every Chakra `<Button>` in the app, base SFCC components included** — carrying `BTN_HEIGHT_LG = '50px'`, `BTN_HEIGHT_SM = '41px'`, `BTN_PADDING_Y = '5px'` at `:205-207`. Those are the provisional values still pending UI-designer sign-off, and they are now squad-reviewed.

To the branch's credit, `overrideStyling.md:191` states this openly. It's a documented open gap, not a hidden one. But it is open.

A separate oddity worth noting independently of governance: app-wide button styling now lives filed under a single atom's folder.

### 3. Enforcement is inverted

| Rule | Stakes | Gated? |
|---|---|---|
| Bare token key in a **recipe** | doc itself calls it *"house style, not correctness"* | ✅ every `npm run test` |
| Trap (a)/(b) in **JSX** | silently wrong rendered output | ❌ nothing |
| Raw hex/px (`audit:tokens`) | real design drift | ❌ manual |
| `npm run lint` | red today, 19 errors | ❌ **nothing** |
| `tsc --noEmit` | type safety | ❌ **nothing** |

The strongest mechanical gate in the repo now sits on the one rule its own documentation describes as not being about correctness. Combined with `passWithNoTests: true`, the harness reports green in several distinct failure modes.

### 4. Contentful is on the critical path twice, client-side

- **`footerConfig`** — official SDK client, `useEffect`, `include: 3`.
- **`uiCopy`** — hand-rolled raw `fetch` with the token in the **query string**, mounted app-wide at `_app-config/index.tsx:161`, so it fires on **every page of every storefront**, uncached, with **no `limit`**.

That last point is the most likely production surprise in the branch. Contentful's CDA defaults to `limit=100`. **At the 101st `uiCopy` entry, entries silently drop out of the response** and every key in the dropped tail renders its English fallback — no error, no warning, and a green test suite, because the tests mock the hook and structurally cannot catch it. It will present to whoever hits it as *"my CMS change didn't take effect."*

Both fetches are client-only, neither passes a locale, and neither supports preview on the footer path — so an editor cannot preview draft footer content at all.

This is a project with an LCP budget of ≤2s at p75 mobile, and this adds two uncached CDA round-trips to every page.

Also: the `.catch` in `footer/index.tsx:193` swallows the error with **no logging and no telemetry.** A Contentful outage that blanks the footer on every page of every storefront produces zero signal. There's no project logger yet, so this is partly a missing primitive — but the net effect today is a silent, invisible failure mode.

### 5. The branch wrote the rules it complies with

- `testing.md`'s new own-test-file rule cites `zimmSubscribeSection/index.test.tsx` as its reference implementation — added in the same branch.
- `components.md`'s container/presentational exception names `useUiCopy` — the hook added in the same branch.
- The co-location rule was written, then its own cited counter-example moved out from behind the gate a day later.

None of it is unreasonable, and every piece is argued in the open — which is materially better than silent drift. But the Tier 1 approval is **self-asserted in a commit message**, no human reviewer trailer appears anywhere, and **none of it has been reviewed**: the last review on PR #59 predates all 14 commits and now reads `DISMISSED`.

### 6. The footer left the server-rendered HTML

This is the largest behavioural change in the branch and it appears in **no commit message**.

The evidence chain, verified directly: the fetch is in a `useEffect`; `footer/index.tsx:202` returns `null` when `footerData` is falsy; `footerData` is `null` on the server because effects don't run during `renderToString`; and there is no `getProps` anywhere in the footer path.

Two consequences on a storefront whose brief explicitly says it must be SEO-friendly:

- **Every footer link left the initial HTML** — including the entire legal set. The footer internal-link graph is now JS-dependent for crawlers.
- **A full-height footer inserts post-hydration with no skeleton** reserving space.

`getProps` was the available alternative, and the codebase already knows about it — `pages/experience/index.tsx:54` notes *"A real 404 needs SSR prefetch (getProps) — tracked separately."*

Separately: a Contentful blip now blanks Privacy Policy, Terms, Accessibility, Modern Slavery and Cookie Settings. That fail-closed choice is deliberate and documented, and it satisfies the letter of graceful degradation. But it was made **in a commit, not in a PRD**, and it deserves ratifying or reversing consciously.

---

## Also worth knowing

**`overrideStyling.md` now contradicts itself, and the test suite enforces against one half.** I verified this directly. Line 16 says *"**Never** a bare Chakra/theme token string."* 120 lines later, in a section with **zero hunks touched** in this range, `:137-140` still says:

> reference it **by name** in the theme config (`marginBottom: 'xs'`, not `marginBottom: 2` or `marginBottom: '0.5rem'`)

`marginBottom` is in the new guard's `SPACE_PROPS` (line 100) and `'xs'` is in `SPACING_KEYS`. **A developer following §137 inside a registered recipe fails `npm run test`.** The same section also cites `theme/components/imageGallery.ts` and `swatchGroup.ts` as its exemplars — neither file exists, and neither existed before this range either.

**The `audit:tokens` allow-list has no word boundaries.** The marker regex is `/provisional|pending|placeholder|audit-allow/i`, so a comment reading *"depending on the viewport"* matches `pending` and silences every raw literal in its contiguous block. Latent today; live-fire the moment someone writes it.

**The escape hatch is prose, self-service and unreviewed.** `466e62b`'s own remedy for `zimmButton.css.ts` was to **reword a comment** — adding "PROVISIONAL" and "pending sign-off" — while `'50px'`/`'41px'`/`'5px'` stayed exactly as they were. Legitimate in that instance, since it *is* the documented Handover conflict. But it demonstrates the gate is satisfied by editing prose rather than a value.

**`.docs/memory/projectState.md` is stale in a way that matters.** Its `Last updated:` stamp still reads 2026-08-18, it still asserts *"`button.ts` established as the single source of truth for button styling"* (a file that no longer exists), it still describes *"per-component overrides in `overrides/app/theme/components/`"* with no mention of co-location, and **the footer / SFCC-55 work does not appear anywhere** in "What's Complete" or "In Progress." `sprintScope.md` wasn't touched at all.

**`uiCopyProvider/` has no `.stories.tsx`**, which `components.md`'s Storybook section requires for anything exported from a folder under `overrides/app/components/`. Defensible for a component rendering no UI — but it's an unstated exemption, and the doc pass that added two other carve-outs didn't add this one.

**`en-CA` is never created in Contentful.** `bootstrapSpace.mjs` creates 9 locales; `SUPPORTED_LOCALES` has 10. The missing one is `en-CA` — the ZimmermannUSIntl locale — while `seedRegions.mjs` creates `region-ZimmermannUSIntl` with `locale: 'en-CA'`. Invisible today only because nothing passes a locale. It bites the moment locale-aware fetching lands.

## The three highest-value open items

**1. Fix `overrideStyling.md:137-140`.**

Highest value per minute in the entire set. One stale section is actively instructing a pattern that `npm run test` now blocks, and pointing at two files that don't exist as proof. Every other item on this list costs a decision or a build; this one costs a paragraph edit. Until it's fixed, the rules file will keep sending developers into a failing suite — and it's Tier 1, so it needs the approval route regardless of how small the change is.

**2. Add an SVG stub to `vitest.config.ts`.**

Vitest has no SVG handling, so anything transitively importing `ZimmIcon` throws. There are already three `vi.mock('…zimmIcon')` calls and a *rule* now mandating more of them. That's a compounding boilerplate tax on every future test, and it makes every icon-consuming component's rendered output partly unobservable. One alias or stub plugin removes it permanently. It's Tier 1 test config and you hold tier-1-approver — so this is cheap, high-leverage, and squarely yours to authorise.

**3. Decide the SSR question consciously.**

The footer leaving the server-rendered HTML is the largest behavioural change in the branch, it appears in no commit message, and it lands on a storefront whose brief names SEO explicitly. `getProps` was available. This isn't a code-cleanliness question — it's a product and SEO call that needs a named decision-maker and, given the graceful-degradation angle, probably a line in a PRD rather than a commit body. It's third only because it needs a decision rather than a keystroke; by impact it's first.
